stages.grade_reasons: What 1.2.109 said E62 delivers works on 1.2.118 by reading and by its nine tier-1 tests, all ok in the base run (R3708-R3713, R3728-R3730: tier01.log lines 1617-1620, 1622, 1625, 1627-1629; R3727, stamped E94, line 1626), and the notes' own known gap of two flash sequences on one screen was closed in 1.2.112 (R4652, line read in transitions.mjs:207-213). Not higher, for four reasons. The stage's plan is delivered in part: C7 (texture through a turn) is measured only, with one reading far under its bar and the owner's choice still open, C6 is built in part, the rest of C8 is not done. The main promise as a player sees it - a turn drawn in its direction, six flashes with their sound - is driven only up to the hint handed to the curtain; the drawn turn is the glass sweep's (outside CI) and LIVE-E62-01, unread. One promise is held by reading alone: the Pane flash sound once per onset. And the flashes' share of the screen, which the plan meant to hold against the flash limit, has no measurement. No defect of E62's own was found; on a bystander's browser during an incident the handler still runs (the hint and the Escape hold, nothing drawn) - the visible part of that is E94's (finding E94-1).

findings.title: A Spectator has no Stop on its sheet, and with no GM answering its safeword press is refused by its own chat block while the press reports the card as posted
findings.what_happens: Since E92 C5 (e08aaecc) sheetMode answers safeword false for a Spectator, so its sheet draws no Stop button; the doors left are the keybinding, unbound until the table picks a key, and the API. When a Spectator does press with no GM connected, callSafeword posts the public card from that browser (safewordPoster 'caller'), the Spectator's own preCreateChatMessage hook refuses it as chat ('A Spectator has no chat.') and no card exists; callSafeword still logs and returns true. With a GM connected whose card does not land in 3 s (TIMING.safewordAnswerMs), awaitCard takes the same road, the card is refused, and the Spectator's notice then adds 'No GM answered in time, so your screen posted the card itself.'
findings.failure_scenario: The table bound the safeword key; p3 plays a Spectator; the GM's browser has dropped. p3 presses the key and confirms Stop it: p3 reads a warning about chat, no other screen shows the banner, nothing is paused. The GM handbook says 'Anyone may press it - player, GM, dead, Monocub, Spectator' and that every character sheet carries the button.
findings.refutation_tried: Read refuseOwnMessage for an exception for the safeword's flag (none: it asks only whose message it is and whether this browser watches). Read the three doors (sheet-sidebar.mjs:913-915 skips the button when the mode says so; safeword.mjs:423-433 the keybinding; api.mjs:839). With a GM connected and answering, the primary posts the card and the press works. Whether the owner asked for no Stop on a Spectator's sheet was not established: the plan is not in this checkout, and R3857's title cites only the goal 'sheet in a spectator mode'. Foundry's cancel of a create when a preCreate hook answers false is Foundry's documented behaviour, not measured here.

findings.title: Once a student is made a Spectator, every card that account posted before is left undrawn on every browser
findings.what_happens: hideSpectatorMessage removes a message's element at every render when its author's account is a Spectator's now (spectatorUserIds on the flags as held). It reads neither when the message was written nor what it is, so the action and roll cards the player posted as a student go from the log at the next redraw (a reload, a scroll back), for the GMs too; they come back if the Role is given back.
findings.failure_scenario: p1 has played Aiko for three sessions and posted dozens of public cards. The GM sets Aiko's Role to Spectator. After any browser reloads, none of p1's earlier cards is in the chat log on that browser, the GM's included; the notes promise only that a Spectator's own messages are refused and removed.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a time or flag test in the three chat hooks and in spectatorUserIds (none), and for a sentence in STATUS, the notes or the handbooks that says a former student's history is hidden (none; STATUS 141-151 speaks of a message a Spectator posts). Scenario 93's 'chat' posts only while the character is a Spectator. A dead student's own Spectator (E62 C3b) is not affected: that account still owns its student, so it is no Spectator's account. That Foundry v14 calls renderChatMessageHTML for each message as the log is drawn is assumed, not measured.

findings.title: While an incident hides the clock, a bystander's browser still plays the day's board when the GM moves the clock into Night or into a new day
findings.where: scripts/transitions.mjs:160-186 (onClockHeard asks nothing about the incident), :140-154; scripts/sequence.mjs:1030-1037, :1155-1166; against scripts/day-summary.mjs:91, scripts/hud-elapsed.mjs:199-213, scripts/clock.mjs:881-890, scripts/boundary.mjs:315-321
findings.what_happens: The clock's hooks run on every browser, and transitions.mjs plays the boards from them with no question of incident-store.mjs clockHiddenHere. advanceTimeOfDay stamps the move whatever runs (clock.mjs:422-425), and while an incident is before Stage 6 the GM's Next time of day moves the clock with no readiness round (boundary.mjs:315-321). So a bystander whose HUD stays frozen, whose time-of-day card is veiled and whose own day summary is held back gets the full-screen board 'End of day N' or 'Day N' with its chime, for the end board a card of it in the notice history as well, and a first Escape taken for the turn's length.
findings.failure_scenario: An incident's opening runs at Evening; p3 is no part of it. The GM presses Next time of day. On p3's screen the clock still reads Evening, and a 6 s board titled 'End of day 3' rises with the End of the day sound: p3 learns the GM moved the clock during the hour, which the module hides everywhere else (the rule cited at clock.mjs:881-890 and hud-elapsed.mjs:180-191).

Checked that the move is an ordinary road: tier 2 E17-T10 itself advances the clock in an incident. At Stage 6 a readiness round already asks every player, so the tell there is smaller. Not run: the finding is traced in source, and R3861 pins that these files ask no viewer.

The secrecy promises read true: the board marks a death by the published flag alone (sequence.mjs:929), the mood's inputs never leave the GM (:1116-1130) and the clock's rule keeps the Overflow's names out. One minor defect: the boards are not held back on a bystander's browser while an incident hides the clock (E94-1), which is the question LIVE-E94-03 left open and no test reads. Part of C5 was never built (scenario 86 not extended for the boards; notes 457-459). All three live checks are unread; the owner's table reports of 12.11 and 13.11 changed the stage but are not readings of its items.
stages.missing_to_10: The boards (and the turn's hint) held back where clockHiddenHere answers true, with a scenario that runs an incident across a move into Night; LIVE-E94-01 and -03 read at a table; the frame cost of a board recorded (scenario 86 or a table reading); tier-1 readings of setClock's stamps that drive rather than match text; the two stale titles.

not_established: The bodies of R3717, R3718 (past its opening comment), R3719, R3726, R3858, R3862, R3863 and R3864 were not read: where a promise names one of them it is cited by its title in the registry and its ok in the base run, not by what its body does.

Tier 2's and the scenarios' results of the base run were not ready: every tier-2 name and every scenario in tests_to_join is unjoined, and 'ok in the base run' in this file means tiers 0-1 (tier01.log) only.

The four plans (docs/dev/plans/E61.md, E62.md, E92.md, E94.md) are on a branch this checkout does not hold. The promises are taken from the 1.2.109 notes and the four STATUS files; what a plan promised beyond them is known only where STATUS or the notes say it was left out.

E62: whether the direction a clock change hands the curtain always reaches the turn that same change causes on a real page. The hint is set from the clock's hook, after the row's redraws (scripts/sync.mjs:474-475, scripts/transitions.mjs:189), and the curtain turns from a 60 ms timer after the HUD writes the body's attribute (scripts/glass.mjs:3644-3655), taking a hint up to 1.5 s old (:2880). By reading the order holds; jsdom draws no curtain, the glass sweep was not run here, and LIVE-E62-01 has no reading. A hint whose own turn never comes (an hour change that moves no accent, a bystander's frozen clock) stays pending for 1.5 s and would be taken by any other turn in that time; whether that is ever seen was not established.
E62: the share of the screen one flash group covers against the flash limit's area. The notes say it was not measured and no later measurement was found in docs/dev, the release notes or audit/.

E92: whether Foundry v14 stops a Spectator's own drag at a wall or a closed door (LIVE-E92-02). The module's verdicts let it through; no reading on a real Foundry exists in live-readings-e58.json, live-readings-other.json, docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md or docs/dev/e39/CALIBRATION.md.

E92: whether the owner asked for no Stop on a Spectator's sheet (finding E92-1), and whether the owner's 'Dostaje tylko koniec dnia i nastroj szkoly' of 12.11.2026 meant that a Spectator gets no start-of-day board. The code plays everybody's start board on a Spectator's browser (scripts/sequence.mjs:1030-1037, :1213-1214) and no test reads it.

E92-1 and E92-2 rest on two Foundry behaviours not measured here: a preCreateChatMessage hook that answers false cancels the create without an error, and renderChatMessageHTML is called for each message as the chat log is drawn. The harness models the first (scenario 93 'chat' reads a refused message); neither is a table reading.

E61: the geometry of the entry beyond the three recorded GM cuts of R3703, R3716 and R3718 (1600x900, 1366x768, 1440x900). Other sizes and a player's cut were read by the stage in Chromium (docs/dev/e61/STATUS.md:65-103), not by a test in CI and not here.

E94-1 was traced in source, not run: no scenario moves the clock into Night while an incident's opening or fight runs with a bystander's browser watched (scenario 69 has no incident). How often a table advances the clock inside an incident before Stage 6 is the table's; tier 2 E17-T10 shows the road is a supported one.

No recorded reading on a real Foundry exists for any of the eleven live items of these four stages (items 496-506). The owner's reports from a real table on 1.2.109 and 1.2.112 (the entry's blink, the boards missing on the Morning Eclipse's end, the closed curtain and the scene) are quoted in code comments, test comments and later notes; of them only LIVE-113R-01 is in live-readings-other.json, and none is a reading of items 496-506.
